question: Why is no further division stated in the exposition of the mudrās?
premises: The exposition of the mudrās declares divisions of the kalās.
Its scope runs from the thirty-two principles up to Īśa.
Within that scope the matter is already very clear.
inference: Because the exposition from the thirty-two principles to Īśa is already clear, no further division is stated there.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of dvātriṃśatattvādīśākhyātprabhṛti is compressed and may reflect a technical doctrinal range.
plain_english: In the exposition of the mudrās, the divisions of the kalās are declared; and because the treatment from the thirty-two principles up to Īśa is already very clear, no further division is added.
